metadata.title: जब ऐसे ही जीना है तो आदिम जनजाति कहने में क्या बुराई है | Frozen in Time: PVTGs of Chhattisgarh
metadata.description:
Pando, Pahadi Korwa and Birhor are among the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) of Chhattisgarh—communities whose very existence is under threat. Scattered across forested and remote regions, these tribes live on the margins of development, facing shrinking populations, loss of traditional livelihoods, displacement from ancestral lands, and limited access to health, education, and basic rights.

While India prepares to celebrate the vision of a “Developed Nation” by 2047, for PVTGs like the Pando and Pahadi Korwa, time appears to have stood still—or worse, moved backward. Roads, schools, hospitals, and welfare schemes often fail to reach them, and policies framed in distant capitals rarely reflect their lived realities. As modern India races ahead, these ancient communities continue to struggle for survival, dignity, and recognition.

Their story raises a crucial question: can a nation truly call itself developed if its most vulnerable indigenous communities are pushed to the brink of disappearance?
